cards.heading: Objects and key/value pairs
cards.body: JSON data is built from objects: curly braces holding key/value pairs separated by commas. Keys are always strings in double quotes, followed by a colon.

cards.heading: Value types
cards.body: A value is a string ("text" in double quotes), a number (42, 3.5, no quotes), a boolean (true or false, lowercase), null, an array ([ ] an ordered list) or another object. Those six are the only types. There's no date type: dates are sent as strings such as "2026-11-04T10:00:00Z". Note that "true" in quotes is a string, and True with a capital T is Python, not JSON.

cards.heading: Nesting and reading paths
cards.body: Objects and arrays nest, so you follow a path one step at a time. interfaces[1].ipv4.address means: the key interfaces, its second item (arrays count from 0), then ipv4, then address. When counting the key/value pairs of an object, only count its own keys: the values inside a nested array or object don't count at that level.

cards.heading: Strict rules
cards.body: Double quotes only, never single. A comma between items but not after the last one. Lowercase true/false/null. No comments. Whitespace and line breaks don't matter. Other formats carry the same kinds of data: XML uses tags, and YAML (used by Ansible) uses indentation instead of braces.
